full_judgment: 38.  The impugned Rules are directed to certain problems, made manifest by experience, in the service of the Republic, in the years following the liberation war, and in order to sustain the presumption of its constitutionality the court may take into consideration the background of the legislation. The Rules have remedied an anomalous situation where some freedom fighters had already received some benefits as it appears from the Memorandum dated 18th March, 1978 and as it is indicated in Rule 6, and some others could not be granted similar benefits for want of necessary rules. The rules have laid down reasonable guidelines for election or identification of freedom fighters so that certain benefits may be extended uniformly without picking and choosing, to all Government servants who come within rule 3. The differentia laid down in the Rules are reasonable and they flow from actions, abstentions or sufferings of the Government servants in the service of, and for the cause of, the Government of Bangladesh. The Rules have nexus with the purpose of regulation of the conditions of service of the persons who were in the employment of Pakistan, and now, in the service of the Republic.
